definitions.definition: StockCharts calls the Double Bottom Reversal a bullish reversal pattern. It has two troughs in a row at roughly the same level with a moderate peak between them. It forms after a downtrend lasting several months and usually marks an intermediate or long-term change in trend. Bulkowski (Adam & Eve variant) adds that the pattern is valid only once price closes above the peak between the two bottoms.
identification_rules: Prior trend: a significant downtrend of several months should already be in place.
The first trough marks the lowest point of the current trend.
An advance of 10-20% follows the first trough and forms the reaction peak.
The second trough should form a low within 3% of the first low. At least about four weeks between the lows is preferable.
Volume and buying pressure should accelerate on the advance off the second trough. CMF, OBV and Accumulation/Distribution can help show this.
Price target: add the distance from the resistance breakout down to the trough lows to the breakout price.
definitions.confirmation: The pattern is complete only when price breaks resistance at the highest point between the two troughs, ideally on higher volume or with a faster rise. Bulkowski says to wait for a close above the peak between the valleys; if you don't wait, there's a 48% chance price keeps falling without confirming. Broken resistance can then act as support, and that level may be retested (a throwback).
definitions.key_quote: Breaking resistance from the highest point between the troughs completes the Double Bottom Reversal.

definitions.definition: StockCharts calls the Double Top Reversal a bearish reversal pattern. It has two peaks in a row at roughly the same level with a moderate trough between them. It forms after an uptrend lasting several months and marks at least an intermediate-term change from a bullish to a bearish trend. Bulkowski adds that the pattern is valid only when price closes below the lowest valley between the peaks.
identification_rules: Prior trend: a significant uptrend of several months should already be in place.
The first peak marks the highest point of the current trend.
A decline of about 10-20% follows the first peak and forms the trough. Volume on this decline is usually inconsequential.
The second peak rises to the earlier high on low volume, usually within 3% of it. The peaks should be about a month apart; the norm is one to three months.
The decline from the second peak should show expanding volume or a faster drop, sometimes with gaps.
Price target: subtract the distance from the support break up to the peak from the support-break price.
definitions.confirmation: The pattern is complete only when price breaks support at the lowest point between the peaks, with higher volume or a faster drop. A price filter (e.g. a 3% break) or a time filter (e.g. the break holding for three days) can screen out false breaks. Bulkowski says to wait for a close below the valley floor. Broken support can become resistance and may be retested with a rally.
definitions.key_quote: Breaking support from the lowest point between the peaks completes the Double Top Reversal.

definitions.definition: A double moving average crossover uses one shorter and one longer moving average. A bullish crossover, called a golden cross, happens when the shorter average crosses above the longer one; the opposite cross is a death cross. Using a 50-day and 200-day SMA makes it a medium- to long-term signal.
identification_rules: Plot a relatively short moving average and a relatively long one, e.g. the 50-day and 200-day SMA or EMA.
Golden cross: the shorter average crosses above the longer average.
Death cross: the shorter average crosses below the longer average.
MACD turns positive during a golden cross. MACD(50,200,1) or the PPO can measure the crossover.
The longer the moving averages, the later the signals.
definitions.confirmation: Crossovers often whipsaw when there is no strong trend. A price or time filter can help, such as requiring the cross to last three days or to exceed a set amount before acting. The signal works best when a strong trend takes hold.
definitions.key_quote: A bullish crossover occurs when the shorter moving average crosses above the longer moving average. This is also known as a golden cross.

definitions.definition: A rising wedge starts wide at the bottom and narrows as prices rise, slopes upward, and has a bearish bias. It can act as a reversal pattern (sloping up with the trend) or a continuation pattern (sloping up against a downtrend). StockCharts says rising wedges are bearish whichever type they are. Bulkowski describes a narrowing, rising triangle shape whose breakout is downward 60% of the time, and calls downward breakouts among the worst-performing patterns.
identification_rules: The upper resistance line needs at least two higher reaction highs, ideally three.
The lower support line needs at least two higher reaction lows.
The two lines converge, and the support line is steeper than the resistance line, so rallies shrink and momentum fades.
Volume ideally declines as the wedge develops. Bulkowski says it trends downward 79% of the time until the breakout.
Bulkowski: at least five trendline touches (3 on one line, 2 on the other) and a minimum duration of 3 weeks, otherwise it's a pennant.
There is no measuring technique for a price target.
definitions.confirmation: StockCharts: bearish confirmation comes only when the support line is broken convincingly, sometimes best after a break of the previous reaction low. More volume on the break adds confirmation, and a rally may retest the new resistance. Bulkowski: the pattern is valid when price closes outside one of the trendlines; the breakout can go either way but is downward 60% of the time.
definitions.key_quote: Regardless of the type (reversal or continuation), rising wedges are bearish.

definitions.definition: Support levels can come from previous reaction lows, and resistance levels from previous reaction highs. When either level breaks, the balance of supply and demand has changed: a resistance breakout means buyers have the upper hand, and a support break means sellers have won. Support and resistance are close to mirror images of each other.
identification_rules: Support is established with previous reaction lows.
Resistance is established with previous reaction highs.
A level gains validity with repeated tests in which price fails to break it.
Prices can briefly overshoot a level, so traders often use zones rather than exact prices.
Broken support can turn into resistance, and broken resistance can turn into support.
definitions.confirmation: A level is confirmed when price tests it and fails to break through. A convincing break shows that supply or demand has shifted, and the broken level is often retested from the other side.
definitions.key_quote: A resistance breakout signals that the bulls (demand) have gained the upper hand, and a support break signals that the bears (supply) have won the battle.

definitions.definition: A downtrend line has a negative slope and is drawn by connecting two or more highs, each lower than the one before. It acts as resistance and shows that net supply is increasing as price falls. The downtrend stays intact while prices remain below the line.
identification_rules: Connect two or more highs; the second high must be lower than the first.
At least three points must be connected before the line counts as a valid trend line.
The line acts as resistance.
The downtrend is solid while prices stay below the line.
definitions.confirmation: A break above the downtrend line means net supply is decreasing and a trend change could be close. StockCharts notes that a trend line break is not the same as a trend change.
definitions.key_quote: As long as prices remain below the downtrend line, the downtrend is solid and intact.

definitions.definition: An uptrend line has a positive slope and is drawn by connecting two or more lows, each higher than the one before. It acts as support and shows that net demand is increasing as price rises. The uptrend stays intact while prices remain above the line.
identification_rules: Connect two or more lows; the second low must be higher than the first.
At least three points must be connected before the line counts as a valid trend line.
The line acts as support.
The uptrend is solid while prices stay above the line.
definitions.confirmation: A break below the uptrend line means net demand has weakened and a trend change could be close.
definitions.key_quote: As long as prices remain above the trend line, the uptrend is considered solid and intact.
